title: What Else Are You Taking?

patient.name: Mdm Lim Guek Eng
patient.presenting_complaint: New patient referred for cataract assessment; here for history taking and baseline tests

history.hpc: Mdm Lim is a new patient referred for cataract assessment. During the medication history she initially lists only her blood pressure pill. On gentle prompting she adds: 'I take some Chinese herbs from my friend, that one also need to tell you meh? And the doctor gave me a blood-thinning tablet for my heart.' She also recalls feeling itchy and swollen once after an antibiotic eye drop years ago. No current eye pain or red eye.
history.pmhx: Hypertension, atrial fibrillation (on anticoagulant). Cataracts (for assessment).
history.social_hx: Lives with husband. Takes traditional supplements from friends. Non-smoker.

examination_findings.fundus: For doctor as part of assessment

investigations.history_documentation: Complete medication history obtained: antihypertensive, anticoagulant (warfarin) for atrial fibrillation, and an unspecified herbal supplement. A drug allergy was elicited (previous reaction to an antibiotic eye drop). Family history of glaucoma noted.

diagnosis: A thorough general health and medication history uncovered an anticoagulant, a herbal supplement, and a previous eye-drop allergy — all important before any procedure or surgery. This case is about complete, safe history taking rather than an eye disease per se.

immediate: Take a structured general health history: systemic conditions, medications, allergies
Specifically ask about anti-coagulants, herbal supplements, vitamins, and steroids, which patients often omit
Document the anticoagulant (relevant to bleeding risk for surgery) and clarify it with the patient
Record the eye-drop allergy clearly and prominently so the wrong drop is not given
Note the family history of glaucoma for the doctor
Perform baseline VA and IOP, and document the full history for the doctor
follow_up: Doctor to review the anticoagulant in planning any cataract surgery (bleeding risk)
Advise the patient to bring all her medications and supplements (or a list) to the next visit
Confirm the exact herbal supplement where possible
patient_education: Explain that herbal supplements and blood thinners are important to tell us because they can affect procedures and bleeding
Reassure her that sharing this information keeps her safe
Advise her to keep an updated medication list and bring it to appointments
Explain the recorded allergy will be flagged so she is not given that drop again

key_points: Takes a structured general health and medication history
Specifically probes for anticoagulants, herbal supplements, vitamins, and steroids
Elicits and records the previous eye-drop allergy
Documents the full medication list including the herbal supplement and anticoagulant
Flags the drug allergy prominently in the record
Records the history completely and clearly for the doctor
Recognises the anticoagulant as significant for surgical bleeding risk
Understands why herbal supplements must be elicited (interactions/bleeding)
Identifies the eye-drop allergy as a key safety item
Frames the task as complete, safe history taking
Documents medications, supplements, and allergy accurately
Communicates the anticoagulant to the doctor for surgical planning
Educates the patient on why supplements and blood thinners matter
Advises bringing an updated medication list to future visits
